scope.note: Candidate sites must lie inside Telangana, Maharashtra, Karnataka or Tamil Nadu. The ADM1 boundary is a screening dataset, not a legal determination.

note: Catalogue of every source required by the dashboard. The product is limited to Telangana, Maharashtra, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu. A source is PROCESSING_TESTED only after a real candidate polygon produced an observation. JRC and Copernicus STAC passed live processing tests on 2026-10-27. SRTM remains DISCOVERED because no Earthdata token was available for a live run. No source is VALIDATED or INTEGRATED.

sources.authentication: none for the JRC download portal; an Earth Engine account is needed for the Earth Engine mirror
sources.attribution: European Commission Joint Research Centre, Global Surface Water
sources.join_key_or_geometry: Raster sample by candidate polygon and configurable buffer
sources.fallback: JRC GSW via Earth Engine; NRSC flood atlas for India-specific corroboration
sources.next_action: Keep the verified tile path and add a scheduled refresh check; the connector is not yet shown in the dashboard UI.
sources.quality_notes: Historical water occurrence is not a flood return-period probability. Landsat resolution misses small or ephemeral water bodies. Store the release version and report valid-pixel coverage instead of extrapolating. Live verification 2026-10-27: occurrence_70E_20N_v1_5_2024.tif (44,348,023 bytes, HTTP 200) produced five observations for a Pune polygon with 100% valid-pixel coverage, 2.08% occurrence overlap, 0.49% mean occurrence, 68% maximum occurrence and 0 m to the nearest mapped water pixel. Tile labels are west longitude and north latitude.
sources.licence: JRC open data; free with attribution. Confirm the current release terms before redistribution.

sources.join_key_or_geometry: Raster tile request by candidate polygon bounds plus buffer
sources.fallback: Copernicus DEM GLO-30 via CDSE; manual tile upload
sources.next_action: Run an authenticated tile request for a test polygon and compute elevation, slope and relief with a void fraction.
sources.quality_notes: Screening-level elevation, not a detailed site survey or hydrological model. SRTM has voids in steep terrain. Report the void fraction and do not interpolate across large gaps without labelling the method.
sources.provider: NASA / USGS, distributed by LP DAAC
sources.dataset_name: Shuttle Radar Topography Mission Global 1 arc second (SRTMGL1)
sources.licence: NASA open data; no restrictions on use, access or download
sources.coverage: Global land between 60 degrees north and 56 degrees south

sources.authentication: Anonymous STAC search confirmed; downloading assets requires a CDSE account
sources.join_key_or_geometry: STAC search by candidate polygon, date range and maximum cloud cover
sources.fallback: Copernicus Open Access Hub; cached scene metadata
sources.next_action: Add authenticated asset download, cloud masking and median NDVI; scene metadata alone is not a land-cover measurement.
sources.quality_notes: Scene discovery is not a land-cover measurement. NDVI indicates vegetation condition; it does not establish legal land use. Always show the observation date, cloud cover and valid-pixel fraction. Live verification 2026-10-27: anonymous POST to the CDSE STAC search for a Pune polygon returned 90 Sentinel-2 L2A scenes over 2025-10-30 to 2026-10-25 (HTTP 200, 6,285,681 bytes, SHA-256 f643d10c...). Median cloud cover was 13.9%, minimum 0%, and 51 of 90 scenes (56.7%) were at or below the 20% threshold. Only scene metadata was read; no pixels or NDVI were processed.
sources.dataset_name: Sentinel-2 Level-2A scene catalogue via STAC
sources.licence: Copernicus open data; free, full and open

sources.join_key_or_geometry: Region/state mapping; not a site geometry join
sources.fallback: State utility evidence (manual); explicit unavailable carbon factor
sources.next_action: Parse the CO2 baseline workbook into year-by-region factors before using any power-system aggregate.
sources.quality_notes: Regional capacity and generation are not site-level grid headroom. The CO2 factor is an annual weighted average, not nodal or hourly. Use the factor for the year electricity was consumed.
